chunks: From him, from Dawud ibn Rizin, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"When a man says to you, 'Buy for me,' do not give him from what is in your possession, even if what you have is better than what he has."
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on buying an item for someone from your own possession?
ai.summary: In the context of *tahdhib-al-ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of *wakalah* (agency) and *isti'mar* (hiring for service), emphasizing the separation of ownership to prevent disputes over quality or price. Scholars note that even if the agent's goods are superior, retaining the distinction ensures that the principal bears the risk and reward of their specific purchase, preserving the integrity of the commercial contract.
